problem: The pioneering ESSG (Embodied Semantic Scene Graph Generation) navigation policy of Li et al. uses REINFORCE with a tiny 16-action discretisation, which gives unstable learning, degenerate behaviour (almost no translation) and inefficient exploration under a fixed action budget.
motivation: Semantic world models built as scene graphs need well-chosen viewpoints within a limited step budget, and navigation determines what information reaches the model. The paper isolates navigation as an optimisable component and asks how the optimiser, action resolution, action factorisation, curriculum and depth supervision affect SSG completeness and safety.
key_idea: Replace REINFORCE with PPO under identical reward shaping and use a finer-grained 504-motion action set with a factorised multi-head policy (rotation, length, stop) to maximise scene-graph Node Recall.
insight: The optimiser alone explains most of the baseline's failure: IL pretraining and depth do not help REINFORCE (S0/S1 about 0.50 Node Recall vs. 0.48), while PPO on the same 16 actions reaches 0.58. A large atomic 504-action head is hard to learn, collapsing onto few actions and giving straight corridor-like paths, whereas the factorised multi-head policy reuses motion components, reaching 0.93 Node Recall with higher Move Success Rate. Curriculum learning mainly improves safety in the multi-head setting and hurts the single-head one; depth mainly helps safety in the compact setting.
method: State representation: frozen ResNet18 RGB encoder, optional depth CNN, previous-action embedding, and local and global semantic scene graph embeddings (HGT) built from AI2-THOR ground-truth metadata, plus a stagnation embedding from the GSSG change.
Action space: SH16 (8 angles x 2 lengths), SH504 (24 angles x 21 lengths 0-2 m, Stop=(0,0)), or a multi-head policy with rotation (24), length (21) and binary Stop heads; move-first execution.
Dense reward: potential-based shaping S_t (node recall, visibility, viewpoint diversity, time penalty) plus event terms for collision, move success, discovery and stop; identical across all variants.
Policy and training: two-layer LSTM core (1024 hidden), PPO (clipped, GAE, value clipping, K=4 epochs) versus REINFORCE with optional IL pretraining; Optuna-tuned hyperparameters, 5 seeds.
Curriculum learning: staged action-space expansion 16->48->160->504 via logit masking, with plateau detection and an entropy boost after promotion.
Depth collision auxiliary head: BCE classifier on depth-CNN features supervised by environment motion-success signals, trained only on translation steps.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (frozen) + depth CNN + HGT graph encoder + 2-layer LSTM policy trained with PPO/REINFORCE from scratch
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR FloorPlans 1-27 (1000 blocks x 32 envs x 60 steps, 5 seeds); REINFORCE baselines optionally use an offline expert-trajectory IL dataset
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (224x224), optional depth, previous action, and ground-truth-derived local/global semantic scene graphs
setting.action_space: discrete rotation/translation primitives: 16 or 504 atomic actions, or factorised multi-head (24 angles x 21 lengths 0-2 m + Stop)
setting.privileged: scene graphs (nodes, relations, visibility) come from simulator ground-truth metadata with perfect data association

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out FloorPlans 28-30, 10 episodes per scene, means across 5 seeds, final checkpoint
numbers.backbone: ResNet18 + depth CNN + LSTM, PPO, multi-head 504
numbers.extra: 40-step budget; depth with collision aux head; curriculum learning

numbers.backbone: ResNet18 + depth CNN + LSTM, PPO, single-head 504

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out FloorPlans 28-30; reproduction of Li et al. baseline
numbers.backbone: ResNet18 + LSTM, REINFORCE with IL pretraining

numbers_note: Custom ESSG evaluation on AI2-THOR FloorPlans 28-30, not a standard navigation benchmark; metrics are Node Recall etc. (0-1 scale). Abstract's '21% relative improvement' matches 0.48->0.58.
results: PPO alone lifts Node Recall from 0.48 (REINFORCE+IL baseline) to 0.58 with the same 16 actions and reward. Adding the 504-action set with a factorised multi-head policy reaches 0.93 Node Recall with the highest episodic return (1.11) and longest path (12.9), beating single-head 504 (0.92 and only 0.42 Move Success).
limitations: Ground-truth simulator scene graphs with perfect data association, so results are best-case with no perception noise.
Small, structured training and evaluation environments (AI2-THOR FloorPlans 1-27 / 28-30); some configs did not converge.
The larger action space confounds finer discretisation with a larger maximum per-step translation (0.3 m to 2.0 m).
builds_on: Embodied Semantic Scene Graph Generation (Li et al. 2022)
